answer.generated: Traditional RISC instructions use a three-address format where each operation specifies three operands: two source registers and one destination register. In contrast, compressed RISC-V instructions like RV32IC encode common intermediate operations in 16-bit formats, often using only two addresses (one source and one destination) but with smaller fields for addresses and immediates, reducing overall instruction size. This compression allows more instructions to be packed into memory, improving performance and code density, while still supporting many RISC operations through clever encoding of frequently used patterns.
